brief.ask: Create a brand identity for Göçebe, the outdoor and travel gear shop in this folder.
brief.owner: Owner preferences: durable, free-spirited and grounded, Turkish at heart but ready for Europe; for hikers and long-distance travellers. The wordmark must keep the Turkish letters ö and ç correct. No mountains, tents, compasses, trees or arrows. Web shop, product tags, social, and an embroidered or woven label version.

claim.notes: All five concepts across two rounds (dikis, iplik, dugum, heybe, kordon) passed verify but failed the critic's blind gate with next=reject (best blind average 5.6), so nothing was finalized, exported or installed and no gallery was built.

concepts.title: Dikiş
readsAs: a startled cartoon face with eyebrows (owl/emoji)
a bagel or donut with two sprinkles. Unfortunate: a shocked/angry face emoji
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a Turkish ö with chunky dots (stitch is second, faintly); s2 the word-pair öç, but the lone bar under c reads as an underline, not a cedilla; s3 Hungarian ő (diagonal pair) - struck, brief fault; s4 ő plus a slashed c - struck, same fault; s5 a surprised face / robot eyes before ö - struck. Keep s1: correct ö, survives 16 px, embroiderable. Risks: the bars are just rounded dots, nothing yet says stitch - give them thread logic (slight taper, a needle-hole gap where they would pierce, satin-stitch direction) without tilting them; keep them level always. Develop in the full GÖÇEBE/göçebe word so the ç cedilla speaks the same stitch language as a real hook, not a floating bar. Watch the face reading at avatar size.

concepts.title: Düğüm
readsAs: interlaced rings or a Celtic-style knot
a coiled snake. Unfortunate: the onsen/hot-food steam symbol - reads like a restaurant or spa
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 triskelion / Celtic triquetra - struck (known symbol); s2 triskelion / fidget spinner - struck; s3 trefoil knot / squid - struck, same triquetra family; s4 triskelion with a tail - struck; s5 a heavy tied knot / pretzel. Only s5 breaks the three-fold symmetry that makes the rest read as Celtic/Trinity knot, so it is the pick, narrowly. Risks: pretzel reading; rope knots are common outdoor imagery, so ownability rests on making it a specific tied cord (asymmetric ends, one cut end clearly longer, cord thickness reading as webbing/cord). Never let it drift back toward rotational symmetry. The flame-like pointed cut ends should become blunt cut ends. Weakest of the three concepts.

concepts.title: Heybe
readsAs: a domino/eye mask or pair of goggles
a bra (unfortunate for an apparel brand)
an old telephone handset / balance scale, with playing-card diamonds
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 headphones (struck); s2 headphones / barbell with weight plates (struck); s3 a two-pocket bag or satchel with kilim lozenges - closest to a heybe; s4 a shopping bag or handbag icon (struck: product object drawn plainly); s5 a plug on a cable / hanging scale (struck). Pick s3, but its risk is a generic handbag or luggage icon. Any high arch over the band reads as a headphone band - keep the band low and flat, more a draped strip than a handle. Push the kilim weave so it reads as cloth, not a box: give the pockets a soft sag at the bottom, make the lozenge pattern carry the identity (and work as embroidery), and make the two pockets clearly a pair hanging from one band, not two blocks touching. Check it does not read as a camera, binoculars or a briefcase at 16 px.

concepts.title: İplik
readsAs: a C with a curled tail (ç cedilla flourish)
a fish hook or shepherd's crook. Unfortunate: a stethoscope - reads as a health/clinic brand
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 'co' / a c with a ring on its tail (at 16 px the loop closes into an o); s2 a c with a gold ring or earring hook; s3 a calligraphic ç with a hanging hook; s4 a loading spinner - struck (UI glyph). Keep s3: first reading is ç, the cedilla-as-slack idea is closest, one strand, embroiderable as a single satin line. Risks: it reads more as script ç / question-mark hook than thread - the loose end must clearly be a cut thread end (blunt cut, slight fray or finer end), and the loop should read as slack, not a knob. Avoid it turning into a fishhook. Check it beside the wordmark so the ç here and in the word match.

concepts.title: Kordon
readsAs: a lowercase g with its descender cut off (split-g monogram)
a geometric-sans fintech or app logo
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: word-a 'göçebe' in a rounded, slightly wobbly monoline - reads fully as the name, but as a friendly children's/comic face rather than cord, and the square ö dots fight the round strokes; word-b same plus a joined baseline under 'ebe' that reads as a scribbled underline. Icons: s1 'öç' - in Turkish that word means revenge (struck); s2 'eb', a meaningless fragment; s3 ö reads as a startled face again, the round-1 failure (struck); s4 a plain ç in a rounded font, little to own; s5 a g whose tail loops and crosses like a laid cord - the only crop where cord is visible. Pick s5. Must change: make the cord the type's logic everywhere (constant thickness, cut ends, crossings), not wobbly terminals; replace square dots with cut cord lengths or round dots; apply the s2/word-b joining only where the cord truly runs on, not as an underline; keep the g loop from reading as a snake or 8.
